inputs.original_text: The measures follow the passage of Bill C-12, also known as the Strengthening Canada’s Immigration System and Borders Act, which received royal assent on March 26, 2026. The post Canada tightens immigration, asylum rules against Nigerians, others appeared first on Vanguard News .
inputs.modified_text: Canada cannot protect its citizens or preserve public confidence if it treats border rules as optional. Bill C-12 received royal assent on March 26, 2026; now the government must apply it fairly and consistently, rather than backing away whenever critics label enforcement “securitizing.” People fleeing danger, including Nigerians, should be treated humanely—but compassion without clear standards is not responsible protection. A country has a duty to maintain order and defend its authority at the border.
